title: HTTP/3 WebSocket Local Peer Proof Harness Architecture
purpose: Define a repeatable local-loopback peer proof for the existing RFC 9220 WebSocket-over-HTTP/3 tunnel surface.
design_summary: The local peer proof keeps the production `Http3Client` and `Http3Server` APIs in the test path and drives accepted WebSocket Extended CONNECT tunnels through request/response metadata, server ping and client pong helper behavior, client ping/server pong behavior, text exchange, a buffered 6000-byte binary exchange, client close, and server close echo. The xUnit proof wrapper stores TRX/stdout/stderr under `.artifacts/http3-websocket-local-peer/<run-id>`. The cross-process wrapper starts the sample HTTP/3 file server with an opt-in WebSocket proof handler, drives the sample HTTP/3 client in `--websocket-proof` mode, and stores process stdout/stderr plus JSON and Markdown manifests under `.artifacts/http3-websocket-cross-process/<run-id>`.
data_and_state_considerations: The proof remains local peer evidence, not external-peer interoperability. The original local-loopback proof keeps client and server in the same test process while using public QUIC and HTTP/3 APIs. The cross-process proof separates the in-repo sample client and server into distinct OS processes, preserving local loopback transport while proving process-boundary startup, SETTINGS negotiation, Extended CONNECT, WebSocket message exchange, and close behavior through executable sample binaries.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The proof requires platform QUIC listener and connection support; unsupported local platforms return from the xUnit test consistently with the existing loopback tests.
The 6000-byte binary payload crosses the default WebSocket tunnel read-buffer size to exercise buffered frame assembly.
The cross-process proof uses throwaway local TLS materials and permissive sample-client certificate validation consistent with the existing local HTTP/3 interop samples.
The generated artifacts are local evidence, not external peer, isolated-host, ProtocolLab publishable, or remote CI evidence.
risks: The harness can only prove the in-repo client/server pair until an external WebSocket-over-H3 peer is wired.
The proof does not cover production proxy target, authorization, timeout, or deployment policy.
